_comment: Copy this to .terminology.json at the root of the project (or pass --config). Every key is optional. Globs are relative to the directory holding this file; `dir/**` and `dir` both mean the directory and everything under it. Lines carrying a comment with the words `terminology: ignore` are excused one at a time, in the code itself.
_paths: What `audit_terminology.py` audits when it is given no path: the directories that model Quranic data. Tests and tooling are usually not worth the noise.
_exclude: Trees the audit does not read at all: a module about something else that shares a word (poetry has verses; a paginator has pages), third-party code, generated bundles.
_ignore_words: Words that mean something else in this project and are never a finding here. `segment` is an audio segment, not a morpheme; `reading` is a screen-reader reading, not a qiraah. Each one is a decision: write why in a commit message or a comment next to this file.
_allow_gloss_in: Where an English gloss (`verse`, `chapter`) is allowed to stand in for the name: a published API whose field names are a promise to clients, or UI strings, where `display` and plain English belong. Spelling errors and deprecated names are still reported there.
_compatibility: Compatibility surfaces: database columns, wire formats, dataset headers. Findings there are reported once, as known, and do not fail --strict, because renaming them is a migration with a cost — plan it, do not lint it. New columns and fields are still expected to follow the standard: keep the audit running on the files that create them.
